Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

drop

Drop rows meeting a condition

Stata 

drop if x == 1

R dplyr 

filter_out(data, x == 1)

Stata keeps rows with missing x here, and so does filter_out(), which needs dplyr 1.2.0 or later. With older dplyr, use filter(data, x != 1 | is.na(x)).

Stata reference · R reference

Drop rows by position

Stata 

drop in 1/4

R dplyr 

slice(data, -(1:4))

Stata reference · R reference

Drop a variable

Stata 

drop x

R dplyr 

select(data, -x)

Stata reference · R reference

Drop several variables

Stata 

drop x1 x3-x5

R dplyr 

select(data, -c(x1, x3:x5))

Positions work too: select(data, -c(1, 3:5)).

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Drop rows where x is missing

Stata 

drop if missing(x)

R dplyr 

filter(data, !is.na(x))

Stata reference · R reference

duplicates

Drop rows that duplicate an earlier row

Stata 

duplicates drop

R tidystata 

duplicates_drop(data)

Stata reference · R reference

Keep the first row for each key

Stata 

duplicates drop x1 x2, force

R tidystata 

duplicates_drop(data, x1, x2, .force = TRUE)

distinct(data, x1, x2, .keep_all = TRUE) is the dplyr version.

Stata reference · R reference

keep

Keep rows meeting a condition

Stata 

keep if x1 == 1 & x2 == 2

R dplyr 

filter(data, x1 == 1 & x2 == 2)

filter() drops rows where the condition is NA, so rows with missing values never pass.

Stata reference · R reference

Keep some variables

Stata 

keep x1 x3-x5

R dplyr 

select(data, x1, x3:x5)

Numbers select by position: select(data, 1, 3:5). select_or_transmute() also computes new columns.

Stata reference · R reference

Keep variables matching Stata wildcards

Stata 

keep x*

R tidystata 

select(data, varlist("x*"))

Stata reference · R reference

6 more examples and alternatives

Keep the first rows

Stata 

keep in 1/10

R base 

head(data, 10)

Stata reference · R reference

Keep rows where x is observed

Stata 

keep if !missing(x)

R dplyr 

filter(data, !is.na(x))

Stata reference · R reference

Keep rows with listed values

Stata 

keep if inlist(x, 1, 3, 5)

R dplyr 

filter(data, x %in% c(1, 3, 5))

Stata reference · R reference

Keep rows within a range

Stata 

keep if inrange(x, 5000, 10000)

R dplyr 

filter(data, between(x, 5000, 10000))

Stata reference · R reference

Keep the last rows

Stata 

keep in -10/-1

R base 

tail(data, 10)

Stata reference · R reference

Keep rows by position

Stata 

keep in 7/12

R dplyr 

slice(data, 7:12)

Stata reference · R reference

sample

Reproducible random 10% sample

Stata 

set seed 2024; sample 10

R tidystata 

data |> slice_sample(prop = 0.1) |> set_seed(2024)

Differs from Stata R and Stata use different random-number streams; the same numeric seed does not reproduce the same draws or selected rows.

Stata reference · R reference

Reproducible random sample of 1000 rows

Stata 

set seed 2024; sample 1000, count

R tidystata 

data |> slice_sample(n = 1000) |> set_seed(2024)

Differs from Stata set_seed() sets the seed before the sampling step runs, so the pipe stays in one line. R and Stata use different random-number streams; the same numeric seed does not reproduce the same draws or selected rows.
